5198041379.news_topic: Every agency runs your YouTube growth on pure data. I use data plus gut instinct. Here's the difference it made for a creator who was stuck at the same subscriber count for 2 years
5198041379.founder_idea: I learned lesson that experience and listening skull matters
5198041379.current_draft:
Most agencies hand your YouTube channel to an analyst with a spreadsheet.

I hand it to someone who's watched 10,000 hours of creator content and actually *feels* what's working.

That's the difference.

I had a creator come to me stuck at the same subscriber count for 2 years.

The data said: post more, optimize thumbnails, fix retention at the 3-minute mark.

Standard stuff. They'd already tried all of it.

So I stopped looking at the dashboard and started *listening.*

Listening to how they talked about their own content. What lit them up. Where they were holding back. What they were scared to post.

Turns out the data was showing the symptom. Not the problem.

We fixed the real thing. Subscribers moved within 6 weeks.

Here's what I learned from that:

Experience teaches you what numbers can't say out loud. And listening — actually listening — is a skill most agencies never bother to develop.

That's why I only work with 4-5 creators at a time. I can't listen properly to 15 people. Nobody can.

I also do free work first. If my gut plus the data doesn't move the needle for you, you don't pay. Simple.

The best agencies don't just run reports. They read the room.

How much of your growth strategy right now is data — and how much is pure instinct?
